title: Long-running and input-required tasks
summary: Long A2A tasks can pause in INPUT_REQUIRED or AUTH_REQUIRED and resume when the client replies on the same task. Clients must persist ids, choose an update mode and plan for retention and restarts.
useIf: A remote agent's job may run for minutes to days, ask clarifying questions or need credentials mid-way.
avoidIf: Every call finishes in one reply: skip task persistence and interrupted-state handling.

explain.md: An interrupted state means the agent stopped for the client. In `TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED` it needs more input, from a human or from the client agent. In `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` it needs authorization. The client continues by sending a new message with the **same `taskId` and `contextId`**. Mismatched ids are rejected, and a message with only `taskId` lets the server infer the context [[r1]].

explain.title: An input-required round trip
explain.alt: The client sends a request and gets a working task. The agent later moves the task to input required with a question. The client gets an answer from a human and replies on the same task. The task completes with an artifact.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Human
  participant C as Client agent
  participant A as Remote agent
  C->>A: SendMessage returnImmediately
  A-->>C: Task WORKING
  A-->>C: Task INPUT_REQUIRED with question
  C->>H: Ask the question
  H-->>C: Answer
  C->>A: Message with same taskId and contextId
  A-->>C: Task COMPLETED with artifact

explain.md: For **in-task authorization** the agent uses a Task, moves it to `AUTH_REQUIRED` and explains what it needs. The credential should arrive out of band. The spec is explicit that agents MUST NOT treat the state transition itself as authorization, and a credential obtained in that state MUST NOT be assumed to authorize later messages unless an implementation, issuer or extension says so. A client that is itself an agent can pass the request up by moving its own task to `AUTH_REQUIRED` [[r1]].

Duration is an operations problem. Agents MAY expire contexts and SHOULD document the policy [[r1]]. Foundry keeps A2A tasks and contexts for 60 days from the most recent write, and each write resets the clock (checked 2026-10-13) [[r17]]. In Agent Framework, `A2AAgent` returns a continuation token when you pass `background=True` (Python) or `AllowBackgroundResponses` (.NET), supports `poll_task` or resubscribing, and stores `context_id`, `task_id` and `task_state` in the session so the next message continues an input-required task or references a finished one with `reference_task_ids` [[r15]].

whereToUse: Approval flows where a remote agent must ask a human before an irreversible step
Research or analysis agents that ask clarifying questions before spending hours
Agents that need user-delegated OAuth consent partway through a task
Orchestrators that persist task ids so work survives a restart of the caller
Nested delegation chains where an inner agent escalates a question outward

use: Persist `taskId`, `contextId` and the last state wherever the client can restart
Reply to `INPUT_REQUIRED` on the same task to keep the agent's progress and context
Choose polling, streaming or push by duration, and always be able to fall back to `GetTask`
avoid: Do not auto-answer questions on consequential decisions without a written policy
Do not treat an `AUTH_REQUIRED` credential as blanket authorization for the rest of the task
Do not rely on a stream staying open across a long human delay
flips: Retention at the remote agent is shorter than the human delay: start a new task with the answer included
A policy answers the question: let the client agent reply automatically and log it
The credential would pass through several agents: negotiate an out-of-band or extension-based exchange bound to the requesting agent

head: Approach
Wins when

Cost or risk

Client must persist ids and handle retention

Retention is short or state is cheap
The task did expensive work already

pitfalls.symptom: An answer to a clarifying question starts a fresh task
pitfalls.cause: The reply omitted `taskId`, or used a new `contextId`, so the server treated it as a new request
pitfalls.fix: Echo the `taskId` and `contextId` from the interrupted task [[r1]]

pitfalls.symptom: A destructive step ran after the client replied to `AUTH_REQUIRED`
pitfalls.cause: The agent treated the state change or the credential as authorization for the operation
pitfalls.fix: Define and check authorization for each sensitive operation; the state alone authorizes nothing [[r1]]

pitfalls.symptom: Conversation context disappears after weeks or a restart
pitfalls.cause: The remote agent expired the context or lost in-memory state, and the client stored no ids
pitfalls.fix: Persist ids and state, design for expiry (Foundry: 60 days from last write) and fall back to a new task [[r17]]

scenarios.title: A nested question inside a delegation chain
scenarios.situation: An orchestrator delegates a procurement task to a supplier agent. The supplier asks which cost centre to use. The orchestrator's own user is a finance analyst working in a chat session.
constraints: A human is reachable within minutes
unknowns: Does policy define a default cost centre?
How long does the supplier keep the task?
scenarios.question: How does the orchestrator respond?

options.name: Move its own task to `INPUT_REQUIRED`, ask the analyst and reply on the supplier's task
options.why: The decision stays with the person accountable and the supplier's progress is preserved.
options.tradeoff: Adds human delay to the chain.

options.name: Answer from the orchestrator's memory of past cost centres
options.why: Fast when the context makes the answer unambiguous.
options.tradeoff: A stale or wrong inference posts to the wrong ledger.

options.name: Pick the most common cost centre and continue
options.why: A guess on a financial field defeats the reason the supplier asked.
options.tradeoff: Fine only where a documented policy defines the default.

flips.if: A written policy defines the cost centre by department
flips.then: Reply automatically and log the policy used.

flips.if: The analyst is unreachable for days and retention is short
flips.then: Cancel and restart with the answer in the first message.

scenarios.takeaway: Escalate consequential questions to the person who owns the decision.

scenarios.title: The caller restarts in the middle of a six-hour task
scenarios.situation: A caller running on autoscaled containers starts a six-hour analysis task. Containers are replaced several times a day and no state survives in memory.
constraints: Cost of repeating six hours is high
unknowns: Can the caller store ids in a database?
Does the agent declare push or streaming?
scenarios.question: How does the caller keep track of the task?

options.name: Persist `taskId` and `contextId`, then reattach with `GetTask` or `SubscribeToTask` after each restart
options.why: The task lives at the agent, so a new container can pick up the same handle.
options.tradeoff: A durable store and a recovery path to build.

options.name: Block on a single `SendMessage` call
options.why: A restart drops the connection and the caller loses its only handle.
options.tradeoff: Right for jobs shorter than the container lifetime.

options.name: Re-submit the request after every restart
options.why: Simple to code and works if the agent is idempotent.
options.tradeoff: May start duplicate six-hour tasks and double the cost.

flips.if: The agent supports push and the caller has a stable endpoint
flips.then: Receive completion by webhook and still keep ids for recovery.

scenarios.takeaway: The task handle belongs in durable storage, not in a process.

quiz.q: Put the steps of an input-required round trip in order.
items: Client starts the task and gets a working task
Agent moves the task to `INPUT_REQUIRED` with a question
Client obtains the answer from a human or policy
Client replies with the same `taskId` and `contextId`
Agent resumes and completes with an artifact
quiz.explain: The agent pauses the task, the client resolves the question outside the protocol and then replies on the same task so progress and context continue.

quiz.q: A client supplies a credential while a task is in `AUTH_REQUIRED`. What does the spec say about later messages on that task?
options: The credential is automatically valid for the rest of the task
It is valid only for streaming operations
It MUST NOT be assumed to authorize later messages unless the implementation, issuer or an extension defines that
quiz.explain: The spec says the state alone authorizes nothing and scope and validity are defined by the implementation, credential issuer or an extension. Transport authentication still applies to every request.

quiz.q: On Foundry, a task was last written 50 days ago. A client sends a reply today. How long until it expires?
options: Immediately, because it is older than 30 days
60 days from today, because each write resets retention
quiz.explain: Foundry retains A2A tasks and contexts for 60 days from the most recent write and each new write resets the period (checked 2026-10-13).

flashcards.front: How does a client resume an `INPUT_REQUIRED` task?
flashcards.back: By sending a new message with the same `taskId` and `contextId`. Mismatched ids are rejected.
Nothing. Agents MUST NOT treat the state transition as authorization. Scope and validity come from the implementation, issuer or an extension.

flashcards.front: How long does Foundry retain A2A tasks and contexts?
flashcards.back: 60 days from the most recent write. Each write resets the period (checked 2026-10-13).

flashcards.front: How does Agent Framework surface a long A2A task?
flashcards.back: As a continuation token when background responses are enabled. Use `poll_task` or resubscribe, and session state keeps `context_id`, `task_id` and `task_state`.
